content: Severe, and sometimes fatal, liver problems and an accumulation of lactic acid in the blood (lactic acidosis) have been reported with the use of this medication. These serious side effects are more likely to occur in women and individuals who are obese. Although a severe allergic reaction to this drug is rare, it is important to be aware of the possibility. This document does not provide a complete list of potential side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Precautions: Before starting lamivudine-HBV, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. This medication may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. Liquid preparations of lamivudine-HBV contain sugar (sucrose), so if you are diabetic and using the liquid form, closer monitoring of your blood sugar levels is recommended when starting this medication. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Discuss the potential risks and benefits with your doctor. It is important to note that this medication has not been proven to prevent the transmission of hepatitis B from mother to newborn. Additionally, this medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (such as liver function tests), potentially leading to false results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222. Notes: To prevent the spread of hepatitis B to others, always use an effective barrier method (such as latex condoms or dental dams) during sexual activity. Regular laboratory and medical tests (such as liver function, blood chemistries, complete blood counts, and hepatitis B virus DNA levels) should be conducted while taking this medication. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. Different brands of this medication may contain varying amounts of the active drug. Do not switch brands without consulting your doctor. If you have an HIV infection, you should be taking the higher-strength dosage of this medication. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Different brands of this medication may have different storage requirements. Check the product packaging for specific instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
